The yarn is hand dyed with natural indigo harvested from the Tokushima prefecture in Japan. Only a handful of indigo craftsmen are capable of this dyeing technique. It is certified by the Japanese government as a national living treasure.

The lengthy fermenting process required to produce natural indigo and the low annual output make this a highly coveted dye material. The undyed cotton yarns are dipped by hand into indigo dye vats repeatedly until the indigo has penetrated the core of the yarns.

For this reason, natural indigo jeans have a reputation for retaining their color. Most jeans use indigo dyed yarns that are white at the core, since they have not fully absorbed the indigo. The top layer of indigo will eventually give way to the white centers with moderate wear and abrasion. Natural indigo models hold their blue color longer making them tougher to break in, but this adds to their uniqueness.

With a wide range of color options, the 4601 is an easy and versatile piece for everyday summer wear.

Coin-shaped copper rivets, Shogyomujo pocket bags and a specially designed deerskin patch add the familiar Samurai details. As the denim changes with wear, the small red sun remains a reminder of the idea that began it all.

product.body_html:
SAMURAI JEANS — 15OZ SEIGAIHA WIDE STRAIGHT

A roomy 1940s-inspired silhouette meets Samurai’s distinctive 15oz Seigaiha selvedge denim. Woven from Texas cotton with indigo yarns in both the warp and weft, this fabric combines pronounced slub with a depth of colour that develops gradually through wear. One-washed and made in Japan.

FIT & SIZING

The S3000 draws on Samurai’s S3000VXII wartime-inspired pattern, with a mid-to-high rise, generous thigh and wide straight leg. Minimal taper preserves the relaxed proportions from the hip through to the hem.

This model runs slightly small, with the waist measuring just below the tagged size. We recommend sizing up one from your usual size in most American denim brands to maintain the intended fit. The denim has been one-washed, so minimal further shrinkage is expected when following the care instructions, while the waistband will give slightly with wear.

Check our size chart against a pair of jeans you already wear comfortably. Sizing down may restrict movement and compromise the relaxed silhouette.

SEIGAIHA: BLUE OCEAN WAVES

Named after the traditional Japanese seigaiha wave pattern, this denim takes its inspiration from the repeating arcs seen on textiles and ceramics. The motif represents calm seas and a wish for lasting peace.

Samurai carries this theme into the finishing details. A red-painted “hinode” top button evokes the sunrise over the sea, while the jacquard pocket lining features “shogyo mujo” (諸行無常), a Buddhist expression referring to the impermanence of all things—a fitting detail for denim that continually changes with its wearer.

THE DENIM

The fabric’s character comes from the contrast between its two yarns: a heavily slubbed #5 rope-dyed indigo warp and a finer #8 indigo weft, dyed to a darker shade using a different method.

Initially, the textured warp gives the denim its dominant blue tone and uneven surface. As the yarns fade at different rates, the darker weft becomes more visible, adding depth to the developing fades.

Woven slowly on vintage shuttle looms, the 15oz fabric offers substantial texture in a weight suited to regular wear. Both warp and weft are dyed with indigo.

CONSTRUCTION & DETAILS

Samurai finishes the jeans with hammered copper rivets engraved with サムライ, heavy stitching, raised belt loops and reinforced stress points. The brand’s silver lamé selvedge ID completes the fabric.

  • Made in Japan

That inefficiency is precisely what makes the resulting denim so interesting.

The Studio D’Artisan D4620 GL3 Denim Coverall is built around one of the most characterful fabrics in Japanese denim: heavyweight 15oz denim woven slowly on a vintage Toyoda Automatic Loom Works GL3 shuttle loom.

Originally developed around half a century ago, the GL3 represents an early generation of Japanese power looms. Today, keeping these machines running is an involved process. Replacement parts are no longer readily available, meaning worn components often have to be salvaged from other retired GL3 machines. Even by vintage shuttle-loom standards, production is remarkably slow, with the loom capable of weaving only around 5 meters of fabric per hour.

That inefficiency is precisely what makes the resulting denim so special.

Rather than producing the perfectly uniform surface associated with modern high-speed weaving, the GL3 creates a fabric full of irregularity, slub, texture and natural variation. The finished denim has the rugged, uneven character associated with workwear denim from generations ago — a depth and roughness that is extremely difficult to reproduce with modern machinery.

For the GL3 Series, Studio D’Artisan went further than simply putting denim through an old loom. The brand developed its own carefully calibrated recipe, experimenting with the texture and count of the yarns, the shade of the rope-dyed indigo, and the warp and weft density. Numerous test weavings were carried out before arriving at the final fabric.

The result is a 15oz GL3 selvedge denim with a distinctly vintage hand and pronounced surface character. The unevenness is intentional: every slub, irregularity and subtle variation contributes to the personality of the cloth. The denim is designed to develop further with wear, rewarding the owner with increasingly individual fading and character over time.

The D4620 itself takes the form of a classic denim coverall, drawing directly from traditional workwear while avoiding a boxy or overly utilitarian appearance. Its gently flared A-line silhouette gives the jacket a distinctive shape, combining the practicality of a traditional chore coat with a more refined contemporary profile.

Details reinforce its workwear roots, including large utility pockets, original Studio D’Artisan metal hardware, selvedge detailing and a leather neck patch. The jacket is constructed from 100% cotton and is available in a one-wash finish, making it easier to wear from the outset while retaining the substantial character of the GL3 cloth.

This is not simply a coverall made from heavyweight denim. It is a jacket built around a piece of textile history — a fabric that can only exist because an increasingly rare vintage loom is still being kept alive.

WHY THE GL3 MATTERS

Modern denim production is built around speed, consistency and efficiency. The GL3 represents almost the opposite philosophy.

It is slow, demanding and increasingly difficult to maintain — but that lack of efficiency allows the loom to produce a fabric with an organic irregularity that modern machinery struggles to replicate. Studio D’Artisan has deliberately embraced those imperfections rather than attempting to eliminate them.

The D4620 GL3 Coverall is therefore a particularly pure expression of Japanese reproduction workwear philosophy: use historically authentic machinery, develop the fabric from the ground up, accept the limitations of the process, and allow those limitations to become the defining character of the finished garment.

At 15oz, it has the substance expected from serious workwear denim, while the A-line cut gives it enough shape and versatility to work equally well as a daily jacket.

A rare loom. An uncompromising fabric. A timeless workwear silhouette.

The D4620 is Studio D’Artisan’s GL3 denim translated into one of its most wearable forms — a coverall designed to age, fade and develop into something increasingly personal with every year of wear.

Combining durability with refined design, the jacket offers a unique expression of heritage craftsmanship. Its elegant yet utilitarian character allows it to transition effortlessly between workwear and more formal styling, making it a versatile and timeless addition to any wardrobe.

product.title: SAMURAI "S710XX19OZ-II KIWAMI" 19OZ SLIM STRAIGHT JEANS
product.body_html:
Born in Osaka and shaped by uncompromising craftsmanship, these slim straight jeans embody the relentless pursuit of excellence that defines Samurai. Founded in 1997 by Toru Nogami, the brand has become legendary within Japan’s denim scene, drawing inspiration from Sengoku-era warriors and their devotion to mastery. Every pair reflects that same discipline — no shortcuts, no compromises.

At the heart of these jeans lies Samurai’s celebrated 19oz “Kiwami” selvedge denim. “Kiwami” translates to “the ultimate,” and the name is well earned. Woven in Japan using Samurai’s original slubby yarn (#4 x #5), this heavyweight fabric delivers a bold, textured character — crispy, neppy, and richly irregular. The warp is rope-dyed in pure indigo, contrasted by a clean white weft, creating depth that evolves beautifully with wear.

Despite its substantial 19oz weight, the denim surprises with its hand. Initially firm and structured, it gradually softens and molds to the wearer, developing a personalized fit and distinctive fades over time. Crafted from a premium blend of Texas and Australian cotton, the fabric balances strength, comfort, and long-term durability. This is a one-wash, unsanforized version — shrinkage is not expected.

The silhouette is a timeless slim straight: mid-rise, clean through the thigh, and subtly tapered from knee to hem. It’s a versatile cut that honors classic workwear proportions while remaining modern and refined.

Details are where Samurai truly distinguishes itself. The silver lamé selvedge ID — symbolizing the sharp cutting edge of a samurai’s katana — runs proudly along the outseam. An iron-made rising sun top button anchors the waistband, while custom copper rivets, hidden back pocket rivets, and reinforced stress points ensure uncompromising durability. Raised belt loops, heavy-duty bar tacks, and extra-heavy stitching further emphasize the rugged construction.

Inside, the craftsmanship continues. The pocket bags feature the “Shogyomujo 諸行無常” jacquard lining — a reminder of life’s impermanence — woven with precision and intention. A vegetable-tanned sheep leather patch crowns the back, complemented by original artwork detailing and a refined pocket flasher. Even the coin pocket reveals a subtle peek-a-boo selvedge finish.

Handcrafted in Japan with meticulous attention to every stitch, these jeans are more than denim — they are a statement of heritage, discipline, and the pursuit of the extraordinary.

product.title: SAMURAI "S0710XX-WASHI" 15OZ LIMITED EDITION SLIM STRAIGHT JEANS
product.body_html:

This limited-release denim is woven from a 15oz selvedge cloth that blends traditional cotton with authentic washi paper fibers, creating a jean that feels remarkably light, breathable, and comfortable without sacrificing durability or character.

Washi, a material deeply rooted in Japanese culture, has long been prized for its strength, lightness, and resilience. By integrating washi fibers into the weft yarns, Samurai achieves a fabric with natural moisture control, fast drying properties, and excellent airflow. The result is a crisp, dry handfeel with a subtle cooling effect, making these jeans especially well-suited for all-season wear—even in warmer conditions where traditional heavyweight denim can feel oppressive.

The warp yarns are crafted from Samurai’s own extra-long staple cotton, rope-dyed in rich indigo. This premium cotton brings a smooth texture and refined sheen that contrasts beautifully with the airy, paper-infused weft. Over time, the denim will evolve dramatically, producing bold, high-contrast fades while gradually softening and gaining depth through wear.

The S0710XX-Washi is cut in Samurai’s classic 710 slim straight profile, featuring a mid-rise waist, balanced room in the thighs, and a subtle taper from knee to hem. The silhouette is clean and adaptable, working just as well with boots as it does with low-profile sneakers.

Construction details reflect Samurai’s uncompromising standards: custom-engraved metal buttons, jacquard-woven pocket bags, a selvedge-lined coin pocket, silver lamé selvedge ID, understated tonal arcuates, and a specially produced goatskin leather patch. Each pair is one-washed to ensure stability and consistent sizing, while still preserving the texture and character of unsanforized denim.

product.title: STUDIO D'ARTISAN "D1909 VIETNAM WAR" 14OZ STRAIGHT JEANS
product.body_html:
The Studio D’Artisan “Vietnam War” Selvedge Jeans are a thoughtful exploration of what a true war model might have looked like had it emerged during the turbulent 1960s. Rather than reproducing a single historical garment, this pair blends factual references with imaginative interpretation — a denim “what if?” rooted in military and workwear history.

During World War II, strict government regulations reshaped everyday clothing. Denim production was forced to adapt: surplus fabrics were reused, trims were simplified, and non-essential details were removed to conserve materials. Many skilled craftsmen were reassigned to military uniform production, leaving jeans to be sewn by less-experienced workers. The result was denim with rough stitching, uneven details, and a utilitarian character born of necessity rather than design.

Studio D’Artisan takes this historical context and projects it forward into the Vietnam War era. The brand imagines how denim might have continued to evolve under similar constraints — becoming even more stripped-back, functional, and raw. The result is a pair of jeans that feels authentic, rugged, and intentionally imperfect.

Key design elements reflect this concept. The back pocket stitching is painted rather than sewn, echoing material-saving techniques. The pocket bags feature tiger stripe camouflage, a pattern widely used during the Vietnam War. Iron laurel buttons, an era-inspired tear-away style label, and detailing based on the classic 1966 denim model further reinforce the historical narrative.

Despite its utilitarian inspiration, the jean maintains balance and wearability. The classic straight silhouette offers a timeless fit, while the 14oz original selvedge denim provides durability with character. Finished with oxidized Studio D’Artisan buttons, engraved copper rivets, selvedge construction throughout, and a recycled paper pulp waistband patch, every detail feels deliberate and story-driven.

This is not a reproduction — it’s a reinterpretation. A piece that merges history, imagination, and craftsmanship, celebrating the beauty found in imperfection and the enduring appeal of wartime denim aesthetics.

product.title: STUDIO D'ARTISAN "UT-011" REVERSIBLE VELVET ULTRA MONSTER SOUVENIR JACKET
product.body_html:
This exclusive souvenir jacket is a special collaboration between the legendary Ultraman series and Studio D’Artisan, inspired by the iconic Ultra Monsters that have defined Japanese tokusatsu culture for generations.

The jacket’s design brings two unforgettable creatures to life through bold embroidery and vintage references.
On the front, the ancient monster Gomora, deeply connected to Osaka, is powerfully depicted in the dramatic scene where it destroys the city’s iconic castle. The artwork captures the chaos and intensity of the moment, with frightened Osaka citizens fleeing in panic, delivering a striking sense of movement and scale.

The reverse side features the space monster Eleking, rendered in a design inspired by classic vintage Alaska jackets. Adding a playful touch, the front also portrays Indy and Clipper being electrocuted by Eleking’s electric currents, combining humor with dynamic action in true Ultraman fashion.

Ultraman, produced by Tsuburaya Productions following Ultra Q, revolutionized special-effects television. The series established a unique narrative structure centered on climactic battles between the Giant of Light and monstrous adversaries, leaving a lasting influence on the tokusatsu genre. One of Ultraman’s defining characteristics is its vast array of monsters and aliens—beings from outer space and alternate dimensions who seek to conquer Earth and humanity, clashing fiercely with Ultraman and his allies.

This sukajan pays tribute to that legacy, blending traditional Japanese souvenir jacket craftsmanship with pop culture history. Through detailed embroidery, vintage inspiration, and iconic characters, the jacket celebrates the enduring appeal of Ultraman and its legendary monsters in a truly collectible piece.

Henley-neck thermal made with original waffle fabric that feels great against the skin

product.body_html:
Graph Zero proudly presents the third edition of their 15oz Heritage Jeans, crafted with dedication to authenticity and vintage craftsmanship. Made from raw denim woven on traditional power looms, these jeans celebrate imperfection by forgoing shrink-proofing, twist-resistance, and singeing, resulting in a classic and nostalgic aesthetic.

Heritage-Inspired Design

Drawing inspiration from the early 1900s, Graph Zero’s Heritage Jeans honor the rugged workwear of the era, originally designed for demanding conditions. This modern iteration incorporates thoughtful updates for both style and functionality:

  • Hidden rivets on the back pockets enhance comfort and durability.
  • The cinch-back adjustment has been relocated from the waistband to the yoke for a refined look.
  • A ducktail back silhouette paired with reversed rolled stitching on the yoke adds unique detailing.
  • An offset center belt loop introduces a subtle asymmetry.
  • Reinforced construction with pocket slacks and back pocket patches ensures lasting durability.

With a high rise and wide thighs, these jeans provide a structured silhouette that pays homage to vintage workwear while offering modern versatility.

Signature Details

Graph Zero’s commitment to craftsmanship shines through the premium cowhide leather patch, embossed with intricate designs that reflect the brand’s philosophy. This patch symbolizes the artistry, tradition, and collaboration between skilled artisans, embodying the quality Graph Zero is known for. The engraving reads: "THE ONE AND ONLY TEXTILE" and "JAPAN PRIDE," a proud statement of the brand’s heritage and dedication.

Styling Recommendations

Graph Zero’s Heritage Jeans are designed to stand out, even when worn oversized. For a touch of timeless style, pair them with suspenders and embrace a classic, vintage aesthetic.

Care and Fit

  • One wash finish enhances the texture and feel.
  • Straight Cut
